headlines.article_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu watch now VIDEO 4:13 04:13 Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns immediately Squawk Box Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down as CEO of the chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago and built into a $4 trillion company that powered the artificial intelligence boom, the company announced Thursday. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. "The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," said board chair Harvey Jones in a release announcing the news. The company will begin the search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang and will consider both internal and external candidates, according to the release. Kress also provided a statement in the release, but Huang was not quoted. After a meteoric rise to fame due to Nvidia's central role in AI, Huang's dramatic fall has been even more rapid, following a series of stinging revelations about his romantic ties to a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy. Huang, 63, apologized on Sunday for being "unfaithful to my wife," though he provided no details about the affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, who has worked for a Chinese company and Nvidia customer called Megaspeed. Late Wednesday, The New York Times reported that the Nvidia CEO also had a separate affair, this one with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at the chipmaker. Later that afternoon, The Times and other outlets reported that Nvidia's board met to discuss the company's future. Huang's downfall also puts the spotlight on President Donald Trump , who formed a particularly close relationship with the CEO of what, until recently, was the world's most valuable company. Huang became a key voice on U.S. AI policy while pushing for issues that were in Nvidia's interest, such as preserving access to open-source AI, and lobbying to allow chip exports to China. What investors need to know Elon Musk says it would be an ‘honor’ to hire Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Is Nvidia too big to fail? Its AI financing web raises the stakes : Analysis 4 Min Ago Janus Henderson's Buckley calls Huang resignation a 'clearing event' watch now VIDEO 4:11 04:11 Huang resigning could be a 'clearing event' for Nvidia, says Janus Henderson's Jeremiah Buckley Squawk on the Street Jensen Huang's resignation could bode well for Nvidia shares, according to Jeremiah Buckley, equities portfolio manager at Janus Henderson. "I think you could argue, given where the stock is, that this could be a clearing event for the company," he told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Thursday. Buckley said Nvidia sits in a strong financial position and keeping its strong talent pool remains "extremely important" in the next phase. "We think visibility is extremely high for 2027," he said. "That demand continues to be really strong. We think the product roadmap is solidified through 2028." — Samantha Subin 6 Min Ago Nvidia set to invest $10 billion in Anthropic immediately following its IPO Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic, during an interview at Anthropic's headquarters in San Francisco, California, US, on Thursday, April 30, 2026. Jason Henry | Bloomberg | Getty Images Nvidia has become one of the most prolific investors in the AI ecosystem, and Huang's ouster raises questions about whether the company will continue to shell out capital to other AI startups. It faces its first major test next week, as the AI lab Anthropic readies for what is largely expected to be a blockbuster IPO . Nvidia has invested billions in Anthropic to date, and the chipmaker has agreed to purchase another $10 billion worth of its Class N common stock immediately following the offering, Anthropic said in an amended prospectus on Tuesday. The shares Nvidia would purchase are part of a private placement that will not be registered in the offering, the filing said. Anthropic will list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT." The company is planning to begin trading on Nov. 19, as CNBC previously reported. —Ashley Capoot 11 Min Ago Shares of Nvidia-backed companies slide Intel , Marvell and other stocks in which Nvidia has invested in traded lower following Huang's ouster. Shares of Intel and Marvell both slumped more than 4%, while Synopsys stock fell 3%. Coherent stock also slid roughly 4%, and Lumentum stock fell 5%. Nebius shares dropped more than 19% after it reported earnings, and CoreWeave 's stock slid roughly 9%. Under Huang's leadership, Nvidia has become a significant backer of technology companies across the AI ecosystem. The chipmaker invested $5 billion in Intel last September and said it would team up to develop data center and PC chips with its beleaguered peer. Nvidia also invested roughly $2 billion each in Nebius , Marvell , Lumentum , Coherent and CoreWeave through a series of deals announced over the past year. Nvidia has also announced equity investments in several of the frontier AI labs, including OpenAI , Anthropic , and SpaceX 's xAI . — Annie Palmer 16 Min Ago Trump says Tim Cook should replace Huang Apple CEO Tim Cook speaks with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang in the Great Hall of the People. Picture Alliance | Picture Alliance | Getty Images Trump weighed in on the ouster of his closest corporate ally — and suggested another one should take his place. "NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "A Legend replaces a Legend!" Trump wrote. —Kevin Breuninger 20 Min Ago AMD stands to benefit from Huang's exit Lisa Su, chair and chief executive officer of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD), speaks during the company's Gamers Day event in Seoul, South Korea, on Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026. SeongJoon Cho | Bloomberg | Getty Images Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia creates a new opportunity for top chip rival Advanced Micro Devices . AMD shares were up nearly 17% since Monday, when the markets opened to news of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. As a top competitor to Nvidia, AMD is the only other company that makes a full rack-scale system for AI. Its Helios racks compete directly with Nvidia Vera Rubin racks. While Nvidia's systems have long led the industry, companies are seeking alternatives to the costly, supply-constrained Nvidia chips. AMD's Helios is now deployed at Anthropic, Meta , Microsoft , OpenAI and Oracle . "AMD is clearly the immediate beneficiary. But people need to realize AMD can't just instantly ramp up massive additional volume even if customers look to move its way," said Daniel Newman, CEO of the Futurum Group. Amid market jitters over Nvidia's leadership shakeup, more demand could trickle down to AMD. The question is whether AMD can supply everyone who comes. "If everyone turned tomorrow and went to AMD, AMD couldn't supply. We know this," Newman told CNBC in an interview. Mikhail Svetlov | Getty Images Nebius shares sank 16% on Thursday as one of the biggest publicly traded neoclouds reported third-quarter revenue that beat analysts' estimates, but issued disappointing guidance. Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus: Loss per share: Loss of 13 cents per share Revenue: $980.8 million vs. $907.5 million It was not immediately clear if the loss per share was comparable to the 69 cents expected by analysts. Revenue jumped 571% in the quarter, according to a statement. The company reported a net loss of $37.5 million, a loss of 13 cents per share, compared with $119.6 million, a loss of 50 cents per share, a year earlier. The stock move also comes amid the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , after stinging revelations about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia, which has developed the neocloud market by investing in the companies and backstopping some of their projects, held about $329 million in Nebius shares at the end of June, according to a filing . In a letter to shareholders , CEO Arkady Volozh said the company expects fiscal year 2026 revenue at the low end of the company's $3 billion to $3.4 billion range. FactSet expected full-year revenue of $3.35 billion. Nebius also shared an initial outlook for 2027, expecting revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, "reflecting a conservative approach to the pace of our build-out." FactSet expected 2027 revenue of $12.09 billion. The company expects FY2026 capital expenditures of $27 billion, higher than its previous capex guidance of $20 billion to $25 billion and the FactSet expectation of $23.85 billion. Nebius' expected FY2027 capex of $40 billion to $45 billion came in much higher than the FactSet expectation of $28.77 billion. Nebius stock chart. Nebius' results come after fellow neoclouds CoreWeave and IREN reported better-than-expected financials in their earnings announcements over the past week. That's provided a boost to the companies' stocks, which had suffered steep selloffs in recent weeks on concern about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence buildout. The neocloud companies posted a robust rally on Wednesday, with Coreweave booming nearly 25%, Nebius climbing 15%, Applied Digital rising more than 7% and IREN adding nearly 6%. Each of the stocks fell Thursday premarket after the Nebius Q3 report. Last week, CoreWeave's bond yields spiked past the 16% mark. In its earnings report on Tuesday, CoreWeave told analysts it expects to keep parent-level debt financing under $5 billion through 2027. During the quarter, Nebius said it raised $5.75 billion in debt financing. The political backdrop has created further volatility as Nebius races rivals to open up new data centers. Last week U.S. voters supported dozens of ballot initiatives to restrict the development of such facilities, while Democrats won sweeping victories in both houses of Congress.
